name: La Mano de Fátima
source: Google Maps link supplied by owner; details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Small, lively Moroccan and Middle Eastern restaurant in Santander with many vegan options; chef Nabil Bour-qaiba. Reviewers praise the homemade food, generous portions and couscous (beef or chicken); muhammara with Arabic bread is a vegetarian-guide pick.

name: Alterna Sidrería (Calle Rosal)
source: OpenStreetMap node 10087427219 (ODbL); Asturias tourism listing for the address and website; details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Traditional Asturian cider house opened in Oviedo in 2016 (founders Carlos Pedrouzo and Mònica Gallo), serving traditional Asturian dishes with ciders poured by escanciadores. Member of the Sidrerías de Asturias quality brand; Tripadvisor Travellers' Choice 2023.
hours: Tue-Sun 11:00-01:00, closed Monday; kitchen Tue-Thu 13:00-16:00 & 20:00-24:00, Fri-Sun 13:00-16:30 & 20:00-00:30 (check before going)

name: Alterna Sidrería (Puerto de Pajares)
source: Google Maps link supplied by owner; address confirmed against OpenStreetMap (Calle Puerto de Pajares 9); details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Second Alterna location (Alterna Teatinos) in Oviedo: traditional Asturian cuisine and cider poured by escanciadores; Sidrerías de Asturias quality brand.
hours: Tue-Sun 11:00-01:00, closed Monday; kitchen Tue-Thu 13:00-16:00 & 20:00-24:00, Fri-Sun 13:00-16:30 & 20:00-00:30 (check before going)

name: Asador Llorente
source: Place named by owner; position from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim): Asador Llorente, 1, Calle de San Roque; details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Traditional Cantabrian grill restaurant in Potes with a rustic wood-paneled dining room and mountain views, known for red meat (chuletón) and its cocido lebaniego, described as the star of the menu. About 100 km from Santander, on the Picos / Liébana side.

source: Google Maps link supplied by owner

name: Atypique
source: Place named by owner; position from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim): Atypique, 11, Calle de Castelar; details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Pet-friendly specialty coffee shop in the ground floor of the Siboney building, redesigned by Zooco Estudio; pastries and international breakfast/brunch dishes (avocado toast, acai bowls, chia pudding, vegan banana bread) with a terrace over the marina.

name: Santa & Co
source: Place named by owner; position from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim): Santa&Co, 17, Calle de Marcelino Sanz de Sautuola; details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Relaxed, unpretentious cafe in central Santander for breakfast, brunch or an afternoon snack; founded by an architect and an economist. Reviewers single out tomato-and-avocado toast and coffee.
hours: Mon-Wed 9:00-22:00; Thu-Fri 9:00-23:00; Sat 9:30-23:00; Sun closed (check before going)

name: Kandela
source: Place named by owner; position from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim): Kandela, Calle de Bonifaz, La Gándara; details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Product-driven restaurant with a charcoal-grill focus, meat and fish as protagonists. Guests mention chuletón (especially ox), steak tartare, sweetbreads, ensaladilla rusa, chorizo brioche, flan and cheesecake. Upmarket, modern and stylish; good for dinner.

name: La Bombi
source: Place named by owner; position from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim): La Bombi, 13, Calle de Casimiro Sainz; details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Puertochico restaurant with about 90 years of history (formerly the sailors' tavern La Bombilla), specialising in fish and seafood. Classics: anchovies, marinated sea bass, bonito with tomato, fresh squid rabas, scorpionfish pudding. Upmarket Santander classic for fish and seafood; for a special occasion.
hours: Per Michelin: Tue closed; other days 13:30-16:00 and 21:00-23:30; Sunday lunch only. Salir lists different hours (check before going)

name: Bodega del Riojano
source: Place named by owner; position from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim): Bodega del Riojano, 5, Calle del Río de la Pila; details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Historic central Santander restaurant known as 'Museo Redondo' for its dining room of painted wine-barrel ends. Traditional product-led cooking: daily fish, spoon dishes, tripe, snails, cuttlefish in ink, cabracho pie and ensaladilla. Mid-range, historic, and great for Cantabrian food.
hours: Conflicting: Spanish Michelin page lists daily 12:00-16:00 and 20:00-00:00; other Michelin pages list 13:00-17:00 and 20:00-23:30 (check before going)

name: Casa Lita
source: Place named by owner; position from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim): Casa Lita, 37, Paseo de Pereda; details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Pintxo bar known as 'La Cocina del Pincho' on Paseo de Pereda, with a menu of around 300 different pinchos; queues at peak hours.
hours: Tue-Sun 12:00-00:00; open daily in summer (per Salir; check before going)

name: Bodega Fuente Dé
source: Place named by owner; position from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim): Bodega Fuente De, 5, Calle de Peña Herbosa; details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Long-standing Santander bodega serving tapas and cheese plates with wine and beer; known for its cocido montañés, cheese and croquetas. Often packed, with standing room at the bar.
hours: Mon-Sat 12:00-16:00 and 20:00-00:00; Sun closed (check before going)

name: Casa Ajero
source: Place named by owner; position from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim): Casa Ajero, 18, Calle de Daoíz y Velarde; details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Tapas and pintxos bar near Plaza del Cañadío with a lively tapeo atmosphere and a summer terrace with high tables.
hours: Daily 11:00-02:00, Monday midday closed (per Salir; Minube differs; check before going)

name: Peter & Pan
source: Place named by owner; position from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim): Peter & Pan, 19B, Calle del Rostrío; details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Bakery-cafe with a wide menu and attractive decor, popular with families; reviewers single out the coffee and the chocolate cookie.
address: Calle Marqués de la Hermida 28, 39009 Santander (Peñacastillo)

name: Mercado de la Esperanza
source: Place named by owner; position from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim): Mercado de La Esperanza, 12, Plaza de la Esperanza; details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Historic Santander market opened in 1904 (architects Eduardo Reynals and Juan Moya), declared historic-artistic monument in 1977 and renovated in 2010, with about 80 stalls of meat, fish, seafood, produce, cheese, bread and coffee. A must for local produce, seafood and a proper Santander market experience.
address: Plaza de la Esperanza s/n, 39002 Santander
hours: Mon-Fri 08:00-14:00 and 17:00-19:30; Sat 08:00-14:00; Sun closed (check before going)

name: El Cazurro
source: Place named by owner; position from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim): El Cazurro, Barrio La Arnía, Liencres; details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Coastal bar-restaurant with sea views from the dining room and terrace; short menu with a blackboard of daily fish and off-menu dishes. Known for rice dishes (incl. black rice), mejillones en salsa, guiso marinero, sea bass, octopus, croquetas and rabas. Repsol Solete; recommended by Jesus Sanchez (Cenador de Amos).

name: Casa Poli
source: Place named by owner; position from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim): Casa Poli, N-634, Puertas de Vidiago; details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Traditional Asturian cooking in an 1833 manor house around a central courtyard, open since 1996. Menu: chorizo in cider, Llanes anchovies, octopus, fabada, cachopo, T-bone, entrecote, lamb chops, cheeses and homemade desserts. Ample parking.

name: La Parrilla de Prellezo
source: Place named by owner; position from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim): La Parrilla, Barrio Arco, Prellezo; details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Grill restaurant specialising in grilled meats, good wine and homemade desserts; reviewers praise the aged chuleton (30-day), parrillada, cachopo, Prellezo tomatoes, ham-and-cecina croquetas and cheesecake. Terrace; dogs admitted.
address: Carretera General de Prellezo (N-634), 39549 Prellezo, Val de San Vicente

name: Sakura Santander
source: Google Maps link supplied by owner

name: La Gruta de José
source: Place named by owner; position from address point Plaza de los Cabildos 9; details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Seafood restaurant set in a sea-cave style interior in Santander's Barrio Pesquero; the star is Cantabrian centollo (spider crab), plus lobster, cigalas, percebes, daily fish and classics like rabas, croquetas and Santoña anchovies.
address: Plaza de los Cabildos 9, Barrio Pesquero, 39009 Santander
hours: Mon, Thu-Sun 11:00-17:00 and 20:00-23:45; Wed 11:00-17:00; Tue closed (check before going; site header conflicts slightly)

name: Santagloria Coffee & Bakery
source: Place named by owner; position from address point Calle Florida 1; details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Cafe and bakery near the Town Hall Square and Cathedral with a bright indoor cafe and a large quiet terrace; wide range of sweet and savoury pastries.

name: Vermutería De Vicio
source: Place named by owner; position from address point Calle Cádiz 18 (coordinates as listed on Gastroranking); details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Vermouth and tapas bar with a wide menu, interior terrace and cosy atmosphere; known for the vermouth of the week, mejillones en salsa, rabas, patatas bravas, croquetas and albóndigas.

name: Lastra café
source: Place named by owner; position from address point Calle Santa Clara 10; details from venue site and web listings (check before going)
description: Specialty-coffee cafe-bar in central Santander with views of the Parroquia de la Anunciación; known for pastrami and bacon sandwiches, cookies, coffee, matcha and lemonade.
address: Calle Santa Clara 10 (Turismo de Cantabria lists no. 12; one review says 13), Santander
hours: Mon 07:00-19:00; Tue 07:00-18:00; Wed-Fri 07:00-19:00; Sat 09:00-13:00; Sun closed (check before going)
